candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture generated more than £5.5 million with tens of thousands of people enjoying events across the town. From live performances to food and drink and mural festivals, there were almost 300 Town of Culture-related activities taking place throughout the year. Rochdale was awarded £50,000 by Greater Manchester Combined Authority to bid for the region’s inaugural town of culture status. In a report to Rochdale Council’s Communities, Regeneration and Environment Overview and Scrutiny Committee on Tuesday, Director of Economy and Place Mark Robinson evaluates the impact of Rochdale’s year in the cultural spotlight. The report said: “The evidence indicates that Greater Manchester Town of Culture represented strong value for money for the borough, both in direct economic terms and through its contribution to long-term cultural capacity, partnership development, audience growth, place confidence and future funding readiness. More than 9,000 people welcomed The Herds to Heywood. Image: Rochdale Council “The final evaluation shows that the programme delivered a broad year-long cultural offer across festivals, public art, exhibitions, heritage activity, creative learning, community-led projects, youth arts, music, performance, food culture, film and place-based interventions. “Key activity included Common Walls International Mural Festival, THE HERDS as part of Manchester International Festival, Merhaba Festival, Heritage Open Days, Feel Good Family Picnics, Side by Side, the Poet Laureate programme, FAB Youth Arts Festival, Rochdale Music Stories, Stories We Tell, Culture Quest, the Rochdale Culture Awards and a range of locally commissioned projects across town centre, neighbourhood and cultural venues.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale picked up their first win since returning to the EFL with a resounding victory against Shrewsbury Town at the Crown Oil Arena. Ian Watson's men registered their threat 20 minutes in when Kane Taylor crossed for Dajaune Brown, whose header skimmed the crossbar. They deservedly took the lead in the 33rd minute. Emmanuel Dieseruvwe's shot was blocked and Brown, with his back to goal, fed the rebound to Baba Adeeko, who stroked a right-footed effort beyond goalkeeper Will Brook. The home side underlined their increasing dominance with a second on 43 minutes. Luke Hannant seized on a slip by Josh Ruffels to collect Dieseruvwe's pass and race through unchallenged, lifting a sumptuous finish over Brook from 18 yards. After the break, Joe Gbode fired across the face of goal from a tight angle before Nils Ramming pulled off a fine save to keep out Will Boyle's header. Substitute Jonny Smith rounded off the scoring in the 80th minute, racing through on the right and curling a decisive shot beyond Brook. candidates.source_title: Once bustling, the Seven Sisters in Rochdale is now a very different story - Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: More than 600 homes now sit empty in Rochdale almost one year on from a decision to evict the remaining 228 households from the Seven Sisters. Now only 100 households are left waiting to find a new home out of around 760 total flats. In October 2025 Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) announced they would be emptying all the homes in the iconic Seven Sisters tower blocks , which is actually named College Bank. This came as a shock to many residents still living there, with some initially fearing they’d need to be out before Christmas . Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Landlord RBH later clarified these evictions would take place over the course of 18 months. Just over 10 months later, 117 households have accepted new accommodation. More have left through what RBH called ‘natural attrition’, which means they left through other reasons than eviction such as tenancies ending, moved out of their own accord or death in some cases. This leaves just over half of the original residents in need of rehousing. RBH explained a number of safety issues flagged in a recent building survey meant everyone needed to move out. Structural and electrical issues; problems with the water pumping system; roof damage; and the ever-increasing costs for customers to heat and light their homes were all raised in the surveys. At the time of the eviction announcement, RBH said all tenants will be supported to move over the coming months, with financial support offered by the social housing landlord. Leaseholders who own their own homes would have their flats bought at market value, according to RBH. An update from RBH read: “At College Bank, we continue to support our customers to move into their new homes. As of 26 August, 117 households at College Bank have now accepted offers to move, 82 of whom have already moved with a further 35 making final preparations to do so. “This means that the number of households remaining to rehouse is now under 100.” This update is the latest in a long saga lasting almost a decade. In 2017, RBH revealed plans to demolish four of the high-rises and redevelop them. This sparked local backlash, with local campaigners from the Save the Seven Sisters (ST7S) group fighting to stop the plans. Although demolition was eventually ruled out in 2023, a twist in the tale came last October when RBH put ‘all options back on the table’. After coming out of an ‘exclusivity agreement’ with Legal and General, which looked into a cost-effective way to refurbish Mitchell Hey, Dunkirk Rise, Tentercroft and Town Mill Brow tower blocks, the social housing operator refused to rule out razing them to the ground. Still, RBH says no decision on the potential demolition of the tower blocks has been made. Mark Slater, chair of ST7S, said at the time of the eviction announcement: “This certainly feels like a step back. But as a campaign group we’ll do what we’ve always done, and that is regroup. “I don’t accept that we all have to move out. It’s not a reality I am considering. “RBH, overnight have made a decision to inform tenants that there are some safety issues. No matter how they qualify it by saying they’re not immediate, they’ve now put the fox in the hen house because people will panic. “At the moment they are mounting a campaign of social vandalism. It’s demolition by the back door. “Suggesting the blocks need to be clear ‘before they make a decision’, that would suggest the decision has already been made

candidates.source_title: BFA joins forces with Didac and ROHS for Health and Safety Day - Big Furniture Group
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The British Furniture Association (BFA) has partnered with Didac to deliver a hands-on health and safety seminar, hosted by Rochdale Occupational Health. Bringing together expert-led presentations, live face-fit testing and legislative updates, the Behind the Mask seminar is tailored to specific risks faced by workers in the furniture industry. Ideal for business owners and directors in furniture manufacturing the session is also aimed at health and safety managers, HR managers with responsibility for workforce health and safety and anyone responsible for PPE provision or COSHH compliance. BFA MD Phil Spademan said: “By partnering with Didac and ROHS, the BFA can provide its members with carefully curated health and safety training that is meaningful and relevant. “Behind the Mask offers a combination of practical hands-on experience that is applicable in the workplace, with expert insight and technical detail that supports legislative compliance.” The seminar will include workshops on hearing, respiratory risks, failure to fit and stress in the workplace, along with a session with PPE specialists JSP. Open to BFA members and clients of ROHS, the Behind the Mask Health and Safety Day takes place at ROHS in Rochdale on Wednesday 30 th September. Helen Yates, General Manager at ROHS, said: “Events like Behind the Mask matter because they put people first. “It’s not just about ticking a legislative box it’s about giving employers the confidence and the practical tools to protect their workforce properly.

Baba Adeeko fired them ahead in the 33rd minute before Luke Hannant lofted a beautiful finish over Shrews stopper Will Brook 10 minutes later. Dale goalkeeper Nils Ramming pulled off a fine save after the break to keep out Will Boyle’s header, but the home side’s lead was never under threat and they rounded off a fine display with substitute Jonny Smith firing into the roof of the net in the 80th minute. It was the club’s first win since returning to the EFL and the first three-point return of Watson’s tenure. He said: “I never get obsessed with the scoreboard, it’s been performances that have not looked as we wanted them to look, so it was the way we played, the courage and bravery we showed, that was the most pleasing thing. “We needed to get that first win over the line. We’d spoken about not being anxious and not playing the scoreboard but playing how we want to play and enjoying being out there. “You could see we were playing without fear. The boys want to win so much and run so hard that it can sometimes manifest as anxiety. We’ve been playing with a little bit of fear, being shy with the ball. “That’s been the hard thing for me as a coach, you want it to look a certain way and it hasn’t been that – tonight it was that. Now we have to make sure that is us every week.”

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale picked up their first win since returning to the EFL with a 3-0 victory against Shrewsbury at the Crown Oil Arena. Ian Watson’s men registered their threat 20 minutes in when Kane Taylor crossed for Dajaune Brown, whose header skimmed the crossbar. They deservedly took the lead in the 33rd minute. Emmanuel Dieseruvwe’s shot was blocked and Brown, with his back to goal, fed the rebound to Baba Adeeko, who stroked a right-footed effort beyond goalkeeper Will Brook. The home side underlined their increasing dominance with a second on 43 minutes. Luke Hannant seized on a slip by Josh Ruffels to collect Dieseruvwe’s pass and race through unchallenged, lifting a sumptuous finish over Brook from 18 yards. After the break, Joe Gbode fired across the face of goal from a tight angle before Nils Ramming pulled off a fine save to keep out Will Boyle’s header. Substitute Jonny Smith rounded off the scoring in the 80th minute, racing through on the right and curling a decisive shot beyond Brook.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A care provider’s bid to replace the roof and change the appearance of its offices and distribution centre in Middleton have been refused because they are “out of character” with the surrounding area. Vestacare provides support for adults with learning disabilities through day and supported-living services. The company applied to Rochdale Council for planning permission to replace the existing asbestos roof and external cladding and extend the shallow pitched roof over the whole building at Unit 1 Westcroft Industrial Estate, 582 Manchester Old Road. In a design and access statement submitted with the application, the company said: “The proposal seeks consent for the refurbishment and rationalisation of the existing industrial building including the removal of aging asbestos cement roof sheeting and external cladding materials, together with the installation of a new insulated roof and external wall cladding system. “The existing roof forms are fragmented and visually inconsistent. The surrounding industrial estate contains a range of commercial and industrial buildings of varying ages and appearances. “A number of adjacent units within the estate have already undergone refurbishment works involving replacement cladding and modern metal roof systems. The proposal therefore reflects the ongoing regeneration and modernisation of the wider industrial estate environment. “The improved roof structure and increased internal clearance heights will facilitate a more efficient internal storage and distribution arrangement for Vestacare’s wider care home operations. “The building functions as a central operational support and distribution facility serving a number of care homes within the wider region.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Householders are being invited to delve into the history of their homes. As part of Heritage Open Days, Middleton Library and Local Studies centre is inviting people to the How to Research Your House event. It will give them the skills and tools they need to find out about former inhabitants of their home, explore changes to the local area, and bring the history of their property to life. It could help people discover interesting facts about celebrated architect Edgar Wood, or radical and writer Samuel Bamford. This can be anything from identity theft, online transactions, dating scams and more, all designed to fool you and take your money. “With scams ranging from the simplest confidence trick to the most sophisticated high-tech online fraud, it pays to keep up to date with the latest news and advice. “Several million cases of fraud and of computer misuse are reported to the police every year. It’s staggering, but even more staggering is that so many of those crimes could have been prevented by making a few small changes in online behaviour. “To avoid becoming a victim of online crime you don’t need to be a computer expert. Developing a few good online habits drastically reduces your chances of becoming a victim of cyber crime, makes you less vulnerable and lets you use the web safely.” Steps you can take to reduce the risk of cybercrime include never sharing passwords or personal details and make sure passwords cannot easily be guessed.

Williams brilliantly steered a first-time effort into the top corner from Kane Vincent-Young’s cross in the 87th minute to break the deadlock for the U’s and secure them back-to-back wins. Colchester almost took a sixth-minute lead when Jack Payne’s shot flew straight at keeper Nils Ramming, after Oscar Thorn had delivered a low cross into the six-yard box. Kane Taylor then nodded wide from Dan Moss’s cross for the Dale. But the U’s came close to breaking the deadlock just before the half hour as Brad Ihionvien’s close-range shot deflected wide for a corner when it looked a certain goal, after Payne had done well to carve out the chance. Ryan East’s deflected long-range strike flew just wide for Rochdale early in the second half while at the other end, Harry Anderson’s powerful strike was palmed away by the diving Dale keeper Nils Ramming, before Williams struck.
